before: Some manipulative people are too smart to act perfect. They lead with their wounds, or with how brutally honest they are about their flaws (very disarming, which is sort of the point), and every warning you hear about them just becomes more proof of how deep they are. Your Protector has to catch the moment compassion starts explaining away what you've already seen. "I have honesty issues and I'm working on them" may be a perfectly honest thing to say. It's also telling you there's an honesty problem right now, and knowing about a problem isn't fixing it.

guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
Love bombing is not just “too much affection.” Ask what the affection is doing to your judgment. If praise, private attention, or specialness makes contrary evidence disappear or suddenly exempts one person from standards you use everywhere else, don’t argue with the feeling. Slow the decision down and verify.
brief:
- the main point: love bombing is judged by what the affection does to your judgment, not by how much of it there is; when private attention or feeling special makes the evidence against someone disappear, or lets one person off standards you use everywhere else, don't argue with the feeling: slow the decision down and verify.
- what the dedup leaves to add (group 12): love bombing named and judged by what it does to your judgment; private attention or specialness making evidence disappear or exempting one person from your standards; don't argue with the feeling, slow down and verify, in this situation.
- already in the article, so not said again: "It still doesn't prove you're meant for each other, or that they've earned your trust yet." (Also Look Outward); praise or pity making what you knew slip away (Untangling the Belonging Bargains); P10's "treats it like it's special" (here the point is what specialness does to the evidence).
- stance (STANCE-LEDGER.md): "Slow the decision down and verify" mustn't become cutting contact or trusting the feeling.
